chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar quoted Al-Abbas ibn Ma’ruf, on the authority of Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fazal, on the authority of Zarif ibn Nasih, on the authority of Abi al-Husayn, 'I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say:'
The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) was questioned about the Hour, and he said, 'It is when there is belief in the stars and denial of destiny.'

key_terms.السَّاعَة: The Hour, referring to the time of the end of the world or the Day of Judgment
key_terms.بِالنُّجُومِ: In the stars, referring to astrology or divination by celestial bodies
key_terms.بِالْقَدَرِ: Of destiny, referring to divine decree or predestination

ai.seo_question: What are the two signs of the Hour mentioned in this hadith from al-Khisal?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal*, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) links the eschatological signs of the Hour to a specific interplay between cosmology and theology: the rise of astrological determinism alongside the rejection of divine decree (Qadr). This highlights a Shia scholarly emphasis on how deviations in understanding God’s will—whether through attributing power to stars or denying predestination—serve as critical indicators of the end times.
